messages.subject: Package for Interactive Graphs / Tooltips?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am interested in using R to create simple graphs to visualize data
in a web browser.  None of the graphs I need to make are terribly
sophisticated (simple scatter plots, bar graphs).  However, I would
like to find an R package that allows the user to interact with the
graphs to do things along the lines of:

1. alter color of lines
2. select/unselect samples or series to show
3. show tooltips on mouse hover for each data point to provide use
with more info (like value of datapoint)

This list just gives some examples of the sort of things I'm trying to
investigate.  Can anyone recommend R packages for this sort of thing?
I'm assuming this means the package outputs the graph as
HTML/javascript, but this may not always be the case.

I've come across the following candidates:

RGraph
http://www.rgraph.net/docs/index.html

Playwith
http://code.google.com/p/playwith/

There are probably others.  Any help or suggestions would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: R & Basic Satistics
messages.body_plain:
On Sat, Jan 16, 2010 at 8:40 AM, Rick <rava...@att.net> wrote:
> I recently joined this group in view of my interest to identify an
> alternative to Microsoft Excel and the Analysis Add-in commonly used
> for beginning statistics courses.  Can anyone advise me if R and one
> of its extensions will meet this need?

Using R in introductory statistics courses is a frequent topic on the
(high traffic) list R-h...@R-project.org.  There is a specialized list
R-SIG-T...@R-project.org and you may want to check the archives of
that list rather than plunging into the rather formidable R-help list
archives.  Follow the "Mailing lists" link on the left hand side of
www.R-project.org <http://www.R-project.org>

There are several texts with some variation of titles containing
"introductory statistics" and "R", although I must admit that I
haven't found one that is entirely satisfactory and I have found at
least two that are unsatisfactory.  (If you decide to follow up on
this I can tell you which books I would avoid and why.)  Check the
books link on the left hand side of www.R-project.org <http://www.R-project.org> where over 90
books are listed (most relate to advanced topics but some are at the
introductory level).

messages.subject: Re: R & Basic Satistics
messages.body_plain:
Doug,

Yes, I am interested in learning of the introductory statistics texts
you refer to in your response.  I was particularly interested in the R
book list you pointed out because of my background in physical
chemistry.  Several of the more advanced books look worth reading.

Are you able to tell me anything regarding interaction with an
application exhibiting a similar relationship as that between Excel
and VBA?  I like this relationship but it appears OpenOffice Calc may
accomplish this in a manner unique from the Microsoft method.  I want
to pursue this further as well.

I am actually a returning student.  I lost employment in May 2009 and
I'm taking prerequisites for a PA or DO degree.  Our statistics
instructor recommended Excel 2003 or 2007 and I was hoping I could
accomplish all the goals of the course using OpenOffice Calc.  From my
attempts to perform simple histograms and obtain descriptive
statistics for these to date this does not appear feasible.  I was
surprised to learn this.  I may have to research OpenOffice Calc
further.

Thanks,

Rick

messages.subject: question about reshape
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,
 I have a bit of a problem with reshape function in R.
 I have simulated some normal data, which I have saved in 4 vectors.
 y.1,y.2,y.3,y.4 which I combined a dataset:
dataset<cbind(y1,y2,y3,y4). I have also generated some subject id
number, and denoted that by subject.
 So, my dataset looks like this:
    subject       y.1        y.2       y.3       y.4
 [1,]       1 20.302707 16.9643106 30.291031  7.118748
 [2,]       2  9.942679  9.3674844  7.578465 16.494813
......etc, I have 20 subjects.
 I want to transform this data into long form dataset, but it does not
work.
 I am using reshape command, and should be very straight forward...
 Here is what I use:
 long<-reshape(dataset, idvar="subject", v.names="response",
varying=list(2:5), direction="long")

Here is what I get:
Error in d[, timevar] <- times[1L] : subscript out of bounds

Now, do I get that error because the first column shows me the row
number?
 I have been using R for a while, but not a lot for data
manipulations.
 Any help would be great! Thank you in advance.
 Dana
